290	/// Default value for a prop.
291	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
292	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
293	pub struct DefaultValue {
294	    /// String representation of the default value
295	    pub value: String,
296	    /// Whether this is a computed value we couldn't fully evaluate
297	    pub computed: bool,
298	}
299	
300	/// Where a prop was declared — enables RDT propFilter compatibility.
301	/// The canonical RDT pattern: `prop => !prop.parent.fileName.includes('node_modules')`
302	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
303	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
304	pub struct PropParent {
305	    /// Name of the interface/type alias that declared this prop
306	    pub name: String,
307	    /// Absolute path of the file — matches RDT's `fileName` field
308	    pub file_name: String,
309	}
310	
311	// ─── PropType — The Canonical Semantic Type Representation ────────────────────
312	
313	/// Semantic type of a prop. Rich enough to produce any output format.
314	/// Use match exhaustively — no `_` fallthrough in serializers.
315	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
316	pub enum PropType {
317	    // ── Primitives
318	    String,
319	    Number,
320	    Boolean,
321	    Null,
322	    Undefined,
323	    Any,
324	    Never,
325	    Unknown,
326	    Void,
327	
328	    // ── Literals
329	    StringLiteral(std::string::String),
330	    NumberLiteral(f64),
331	    BoolLiteral(bool),
332	
333	    // ── Composites
334	    Union(Vec<PropType>),
335	    Intersection(Vec<PropType>),
336	    Array(Box<PropType>),
337	    Tuple(Vec<PropType>),
338	    /// `readonly string[]` or `readonly [a, b]`: the array or tuple under the `readonly` operator.
339	    Readonly(Box<PropType>),
340	    Object(Vec<ObjectField>),
341	
342	    // ── Named reference (post-resolution)
343	    Named {
344	        name: TypeName,
345	        /// Generic args, already resolved to PropType
346	        args: Vec<PropType>,
347	    },
348	
349	    // ── React-specific terminals
350	    /// ReactNode, ReactElement, JSX.Element — all treated the same for docgen
351	    ReactNode,
352	    /// React.CSSProperties
353	    CssProperties,
354	    /// A function type: callbacks, render props and event handlers alike (`(value: number) => ReactNode`).
355	    Function {
356	        /// The function's own type parameters: `T` in `<T>(item: T) => ReactNode`.
357	        type_params: Vec<std::string::String>,
358	        params: Vec<FunctionParam>,
359	        return_type: Box<PropType>,
360	    },
361	    /// `Ref<T>`, `RefObject<T>`, `ForwardedRef<T>` and the other ref types React declares.
362	    Ref {
363	        /// The React type as written, without a `React.` prefix: `RefObject`, `ForwardedRef`, `RefCallback`.
364	        name: std::string::String,
365	        /// Inner element type if known
366	        element: Option<std::string::String>,
367	    },
368	    /// React.ElementType — component can render as any element
369	    /// Used for: `as?: ElementType`, `component?: ElementType`
370	    ElementType,
371	
372	    // ── HTML attribute inheritance
373	    /// All attributes of an HTML element, minus omitted keys.
374	    /// Produced when we see ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'button'> etc.
375	    HtmlAttributes {
376	        element: std::string::String,
377	        omitted: Vec<std::string::String>,
378	    },
379	
380	    // ── Variant systems (statically resolved)
381	    /// Result of CvaVariantPropsHandler — the wrapper is fully dissolved.
382	    /// Each member is a string literal value.
383	    LiteralUnion {
384	        members: Vec<std::string::String>,
385	        /// true if this prop has a defaultVariant
386	        has_default: bool,
387	    },
388	
389	    // ── Known opaque patterns (cannot/should not be expanded)
390	    /// MUI SxProps, SystemStyleObject etc. — complex, not user-facing props
391	    SxProps,
392	
393	    // ── Unresolvable — graceful degradation
394	    Opaque(OpaqueDetail),
395	}
396	
397	/// The private payload of `PropType::Opaque`. Fields are unreachable from
398	/// outside this module — the only ways to build one are `give_up` (pushes
399	/// the diagnostic that explains the degradation, then builds the value) and
400	/// `new` (for the one documented exception: `known.rs`, which has no
401	/// diagnostics channel of its own and pushes its own diagnostic separately
402	/// via `known::push_known_opaque_diagnostic` — see that function's doc
403	/// comment). Read the payload back through `raw()`/`reason()`.
404	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
405	pub struct OpaqueDetail {
406	    raw: std::string::String,
407	    reason: OpaqueReason,
408	}
409	
410	impl OpaqueDetail {
411	    #[allow(clippy::new_ret_no_self)]
412	    pub(crate) fn new(raw: impl Into<std::string::String>, reason: OpaqueReason) -> PropType {
413	        PropType::Opaque(OpaqueDetail { raw: raw.into(), reason })
414	    }
415	
416	    /// The sanctioned "give up and record why" constructor — pushes
417	    /// `diagnostic` onto `state` before building the value, so a resolver
418	    /// call site that reaches for this can't forget to explain the
419	    /// degradation the way the old bare `PropType::Opaque { .. }` literal let
420	    /// call sites do.

422	        state: &mut ResolveState,

# 0006. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver, not a leaf patcher

**Status:** Accepted, feature-gating superseded by 0007 **Date:** 2026-09-26

## Context

The structural resolver can't substitute generics through alias chains or evaluate conditional and mapped types. Ten components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 props missing against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) in the 2026-07-25 baseline (`docs/benchmarks.md`). ADR 0004 deferred a fix until TypeScript 7 offered a usable route.

TypeScript 7.0 has no programmatic API. 7.1 adds one, available now as `tsc --api` in `typescript@next`. RDT's own algorithm runs on it and returned exactly RDT's props on 13 components (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).

## Decision

Add an opt-in semantic resolver that runs RDT's algorithm on `tsc --api` and merges its result into the structural one per component. Structural stays the default and the fallback.

- `crates/core` defines an owned-data semantic result and does the merge. It stays free of I/O.
- A feature-gated crate spawns `tsc --api`, speaks its protocol and owns the process. Rust spawns it, in the CLI and the NAPI addon alike. The JS client is not involved.
- We pin an exact `typescript` build and check its version at startup, because the protocol has no version handshake.

## Consequences

- Components the structural resolver can't finish get RDT's prop set without a new heuristic per gap.
- The API is `typescript/unstable/*` and still changing. Pinning limits the damage, but a 7.1 change can force rework.
- The backend costs a process per run, so it is off by default.
- Users need `typescript` 7.1 or later. Without it, extraction still succeeds and emits a diagnostic.
- tsc sees a dependency edit only when told, so `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly, and `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version. A follow-up ADR decides the representation.

## Alternatives considered

- **Replace `Opaque` leaves with tsc answers** (ADR 0004's model). `OpaqueDetail` holds only a raw string and a reason, and can't be built or inspected outside `crates/core`. Some types resolve to `Named` on purpose with no diagnostic (bare generic parameters, TypeScript utility types), so no leaf marks them.
- **Call the JS client through NAPI.** The CLI is a standalone binary that uses Node only to load `docgen.config.ts`, the binding never calls into JS, and the resolver is synchronous rayon code.
- **Node sidecar**, as `config.rs` does for `docgen.config.ts`. It adds a process hop and a Node dependency. It is the fallback if protocol churn outpaces a Rust client.
- **Vendor typescript-go internals**, as tsgolint does. The repo was closed on 2026-08-20 and the API is the supported surface.
- **TypeScript 7 LSP.** Not evaluated further, because the API exposes each query the algorithm needs directly.

ADR 0006 made the TypeScript backend a second resolver that finishes components the structural resolver already found. Detection by shape now covers 92 to 99% of the components react-docgen-typescript (RDT) reports on five large libraries (`docs/edge-cases.md`), and what is left is a call with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`) or a prop a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). Only the checker can answer those: it knows what the call returns. Separately, callisto's rule is no cargo features in shipped crates, which ADR 0006's "feature-gated crate" contradicts.

## Decision

- **Discovery.** The backend may add components the structural pass did not find, using RDT's rule: a declaration whose type has a call signature with a props-shaped first parameter. Each carries the rule that found it and merges into the structural output; on a clash the structural entry wins.
- **Always compiled, enabled at runtime.** `crates/tsc-client` is a normal dependency of the CLI and the NAPI addon, with no cargo feature. A runtime option turns it on and is off by default, so a run without it spawns nothing.
- **Structural stays the default and the fallback.** A missing, unsupported or crashing `tsc` leaves the structural result untouched and adds a diagnostic.
- **Trigger.** The backend runs only for components the structural pass marked incomplete (an opaque leaf, a wrapper call with no resolved props, a callee-added prop it cannot see) plus whole-project discovery when the option asks for it. It is never a silent default.
- **Output.** `ExtractionOutput` gains an additive `schemaVersion` so consumers can tell whether discovery was on. Existing fields keep their shape.

## Consequences

- Wrapper calls the structural pass cannot see become exact without a new heuristic per library.
- Every build pays for the client's dependencies. Users who never enable the backend pay nothing at runtime.
- The checker needs `typescript` 7.1 or later and sees a dependency edit only when told. `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types do not fit `PropType` losslessly, so a checker answer is converted at the boundary and anything that does not fit stays opaque with a reason.
- Determinism needs a gate: a clean run and an incremental run must agree, measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed.
- Supersedes only the feature-gating bullet of ADR 0006. The rest of 0006 stands.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the backend a feature of a separate crate.** Matches ADR 0006 as written but breaks the no-features rule and makes the shipped binary vary by build.
- **Run it by default.** Costs a process per run on projects that structural detection already handles and makes output depend on a toolchain being installed.
- **Add one structural heuristic per remaining shape.** The remaining shapes need the callee's return type; a heuristic per library is what the shape-based detector was built to avoid.

docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md:12:- **Phase 1 — discover.** `discover_files()` walks `src_dirs` with the `ignore` crate's parallel walker, filters to `.ts`/`.tsx` and applies built-in and user excludes. It walks from each directory's canonical path, so only symlinked files need `canonicalize`. Per-file `realpath` calls cost more than parsing on Mantine. The final sort and dedup make the result independent of walker thread order (determinism invariant below).
docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md:19:**Why parallel at phases 1, 2 and 4, nowhere else:** discovery waits on directory reads, and parse and resolve are independent per item. docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md:27:`ensure_fresh()` is for a host without a file watcher. Under the writer lock it compares stamps (modification time and size, plus a content hash while the time is within 2 s of the stat) of the revision's source files, every directory discovery walks, and every resolution config. A changed config rebuilds; a changed directory reruns discovery to find created and deleted files; each changed file goes through `Revision::next()` in path order. It returns one `output_delta()` from the starting output to the final one. Stamps are recorded on the first call after a cold extraction, and anything modified within 2 s of that extraction's start counts as changed, so an edit made while it ran is not lost.
docs/architecture/pipeline-orchestration.md:31:1. Ignores a path discovery would not include (outside every source directory, excluded, not TypeScript): `discover::is_source_file`.

Because the two resulting mappings key _differently_ under Invariant 1's numbering scheme (first occurrence → bare name, second → disambiguated name), they never collide at `insert` and would both silently appear as separate output entries. The actual fix is the `files.sort(); files.dedup();` at the end of `discover_files` (`discover.rs:94-95`), which only works because every path was canonicalized first — an uncanonicalized relative/absolute duplicate pair would sort non-adjacently and evade `dedup()`. See `test_overlapping_src_dirs_two_directories_deduplicates_without_a_duplicate_listing`.

    #[arg(long, requires = "experimental_semantic_types")]
    pub tsc_path: Option<String>,

input.message:
Architecture and semantic-model review of caliper at origin/main 2fc1a4ea (detached in the worktree). I did not edit or commit anything. I ran one clippy workspace build, `cargo doc -p caliper-docgen-core`, `cargo machete`, and grep/wc. I did not run the test suite or any benchmark. Most findings below are stale or contradicted docs. The real design concerns are ARCH-1, ARCH-2, ARCH-3 and ARCH-6.

ARCH-1 (medium, CONFIRMED): the semantic hook can serve a stale checker answer after an edit to a dependency file.
- Evidence: `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:46-52` keys the answer cache on `(component key, FxHash of the component's own file bytes)`.
- The checker's props depend on every imported file. In `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs` the checker builds a fresh small program per request, but a cache hit (`refine`, `cached()`) never asks it again.
- Edit `types.ts`, where the props interface lives, without touching `Button.tsx`. The structural pass re-resolves, but the cached `SemanticComponent` still overrides it through `merge_semantic_props`.
- `crates/core/tests/semantic_hook.rs:170` only tests "asked once per version of the file", so no test covers a dependency edit.
- ADR 0006 and 0007 both say watch must notify the checker of dependency edits, with a parity test. I found no such wiring.
- Related, both low: `answers` is never evicted, one entry per edit per component. Each timed-out request spawns a `caliper-late-answer` thread with no cap (`semantic_hook.rs:106-117`).
- Fix: include the revision, or the component's recorded dependency set from `resolver/deps.rs`, in the key, and clear `answers` on any `update_file`. Effort S, risk low.
- Verified by reading all callers. `WatchSession` (`watch.rs`) only touches `semantic` in `refined()`.

ARCH-2 (medium, CONFIRMED): the batch and on-demand semantic merges are two implementations that disagree.
- Evidence: `types/semantic.rs` `merge_semantic` and `apply_semantic_props` (batch, CLI) versus `semantic_hook.rs::apply` (on-demand, NAPI and Storybook) via `replace_props(keep_unanswered)`.
  - Batch drops structural props the checker did not return (`keep_unanswered=false`) and drops the checker's `react_declared` props. On-demand keeps unreturned structural props and filters by `checker_prop_used`.
  - Batch removes degrade diagnostics (`OpaqueType`, `MaxDepthExceeded`, `CircularReference`) only when every `affects` key was merged. On-demand removes all of them from the answer, even when `kept>0` props still carry their structural opaque type. That silently loses the diagnostic for a prop that is still opaque.
- The CLI uses only the batch path; NAPI uses only the on-demand path (`cli/src/commands/extract.rs:104-115`, `binding/src/lib.rs:167`). The same component therefore gets different props and diagnostics depending on the host, and ADR 0016's "answer equals batch" does not extend to the checker.
- Fix: one `merge` function with an explicit policy enum instead of a bool. Retain diagnostics per prop or per affected key. Effort M, risk medium (snapshots).

ARCH-3 (medium, CONFIRMED): ADR 0007's discovery decision is not implemented, and semantic provenance is stringly.
- ADR 0007 says "The backend may add components the structural pass did not find... Each carries the rule that found it."
- `merge_semantic` does `let Some(..) else { continue }` for any `SemanticComponent` with no structural match. `semantic/src` has no "discover" at all, and `targets_of(output)` only asks about components structural already found. The ADR is aspirational and not marked so.
- Provenance (structural versus checker) exists only as `Info` diagnostics whose `message` text is "N component(s) resolved by the TypeScript checker" and whose `affects` lists keys. `ComponentEntry` has no field.
- A consumer cannot tell per component which resolver produced it without parsing English. After a merge, `inheritance[].total_props`, `notable_inherited`, `discriminant_prop` and `composes` stay structural while `props` is replaced, so they can disagree.
- Fix: add `resolved_by: Resolver` (enum) to `ComponentEntry`. That is a schema addition (no bump needed under ADR 0017) plus a TS type. Re-derive the layer counts after a merge. Mark ADR 0007's discovery bullet "not yet". Effort M.

ARCH-4 (medium, CONFIRMED): module cycles and layering are only partly enforced.
- Cycles: `resolver` and `pipeline` import each other. `resolver/mod.rs:22`, `extends.rs:7` and `mod.rs:301,322,507-946` import `crate::pipeline::{PipelineOptions, HtmlAttributeMode, CollapseInheritedProps}`. `pipeline/mod.rs` calls the resolver.
- `resolver` and `dependency_types` also import each other: `dependency_types.rs:26-27,437,1103` use `pipeline` and `resolver`, and `resolver/mod.rs:319,520,538` use `DependencyLayer`.
- `tests/architecture.rs` allowlists the first pair as "roadmap 2.3" (move `ResolverOptions` into `types/`), and `dependency_types` is not covered by any rule.
- The test is a line-substring grep over `crate::pipeline`. A grouped `use crate::{pipeline::..}` evades it (none exist today).
- `types/output.rs:10` imports `ResolveState` from `global.rs`, so the output types depend on resolver-internal state.
- Fix: move the three option types into `types/options.rs` and re-export them from `pipeline`. Add `dependency_types` to the architecture test. Effort S–M, low risk.

ARCH-5 (low, CONFIRMED): stale claims in ARCHITECTURE.md.
- Line 183: "Under the target watch invariant above it becomes one member of the immutable aggregate `WatchRevision`". `grep -rn WatchRevision` finds only that line, and there is no invariant "above". The type is `Revision`.
- Line 201: "A `#![recursion_limit = "2048"]` attribute is still present in `lib.rs`". `lib.rs` has none, and ADR 0002 says it was deleted.
- Line 201: PropType "serializes through `serde_json::Value`". The `PropType` `Serialize` impl is a streaming `serialize_map` (output.rs:696). Only `CollectedType` and the deserializers use `Value`.
- Line 60: `crates/core` is "Pure extraction — no I/O". It reads and writes disk in `cache.rs`, `dependency_types.rs`, `pipeline/*` and `resolver/mod.rs:611-822` (tsconfig mtime, canonicalize, read). It also calls `std::fs::read` in `semantic_hook.rs:41`. ADR 0006's "stays free of I/O" really means "no compiler process".

- NAPI-side behaviour under real Node, and the TS packages (`packages/*`, `apps/oracle`) beyond type-shape checks.
- Memory and time impact of any proposed fix.
- ADR claims about measurements (Mantine sizes) were not re-measured.

ARCH-1 (medium, CONFIRMED): the semantic hook can serve a stale checker answer after an edit to a dependency file.
- Evidence: `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:46-52` keys the answer cache on `(component key, FxHash of the component's own file bytes)`.
- The checker's props depend on every imported file. In `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs` the checker builds a fresh small program per request, but a cache hit (`refine`, `cached()`) never asks it again.
- Edit `types.ts`, where the props interface lives, without touching `Button.tsx`. The structural pass re-resolves, but the cached `SemanticComponent` still overrides it through `merge_semantic_props`.
- `crates/core/tests/semantic_hook.rs:170` only tests "asked once per version of the file", so no test covers a dependency edit.
- ADR 0006 and 0007 both say watch must notify the checker of dependency edits, with a parity test. I found no such wiring.
- Related, both low: `answers` is never evicted, one entry per edit per component. Each timed-out request spawns a `caliper-late-answer` thread with no cap (`semantic_hook.rs:106-117`).
- Fix: include the revision, or the component's recorded dependency set from `resolver/deps.rs`, in the key, and clear `answers` on any `update_file`. Effort S, risk low.
- Verified by reading all callers. `WatchSession` (`watch.rs`) only touches `semantic` in `refined()`.

ARCH-2 (medium, CONFIRMED): the batch and on-demand semantic merges are two implementations that disagree.
- Evidence: `types/semantic.rs` `merge_semantic` and `apply_semantic_props` (batch, CLI) versus `semantic_hook.rs::apply` (on-demand, NAPI and Storybook) via `replace_props(keep_unanswered)`.
  - Batch drops structural props the checker did not return (`keep_unanswered=false`) and drops the checker's `react_declared` props. On-demand keeps unreturned structural props and filters by `checker_prop_used`.
  - Batch removes degrade diagnostics (`OpaqueType`, `MaxDepthExceeded`, `CircularReference`) only when every `affects` key was merged. On-demand removes all of them from the answer, even when `kept>0` props still carry their structural opaque type. That silently loses the diagnostic for a prop that is still opaque.
- The CLI uses only the batch path; NAPI uses only the on-demand path (`cli/src/commands/extract.rs:104-115`, `binding/src/lib.rs:167`). The same component therefore gets different props and diagnostics depending on the host, and ADR 0016's "answer equals batch" does not extend to the checker.
- Fix: one `merge` function with an explicit policy enum instead of a bool. Retain diagnostics per prop or per affected key. Effort M, risk medium (snapshots).

ARCH-3 (medium, CONFIRMED): ADR 0007's discovery decision is not implemented, and semantic provenance is stringly.

- Provenance (structural versus checker) exists only as `Info` diagnostics whose `message` text is "N component(s) resolved by the TypeScript checker" and whose `affects` lists keys. `ComponentEntry` has no field.
- A consumer cannot tell per component which resolver produced it without parsing English. After a merge, `inheritance[].total_props`, `notable_inherited`, `discriminant_prop` and `composes` stay structural while `props` is replaced, so they can disagree.
- Fix: add `resolved_by: Resolver` (enum) to `ComponentEntry`. That is a schema addition (no bump needed under ADR 0017) plus a TS type. Re-derive the layer counts after a merge. Mark ADR 0007's discovery bullet "not yet". Effort M.
